transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-09 15:00 PST | Duration: 58m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Ethan Liu (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Redwood CSM); Ava Martinez, Liam O'Connor, Priyanka Shah, Noah Benson, Zoe Kim (Stratosphere Capital)

Summary (auto): quick intake on security controls and deployment model. Customer asks for SOC2 evidence, SSO and SCIM support, RBAC primitives, KMS key management options and retention controls. Redwood AE + SE walked through architecture options and next steps for pilot.

00:00:03 Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ethan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. With me is Priya our solutions engineer and Carlos from customer success. Um, appreciate you carving time.
00:00:12 Ava: Hi Ethan, thanks, uh yeah we've got Liam, Priyanka, Noah and Zoe here. We're, uh, evaluating options for hosting inference for our quant models. Security is like, top gating us right now.
00:00:25 Ethan: Totally. Today's goal is to map your security requirements to our hosted/dedicated/private offerings and identify any blockers for a pilot. We'll try to be concrete about SOC two, SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, retention, et cetera.
00:00:38 Priya: Quick note — I might share a rough diagram in chat in a bit. If anything I say sounds off feel free to interrupt.
00:00:45 Liam: Cool. To kick off: we are SOC2 certified internally, and anything we run has to either be on a SOC2 vendor or go into our private environment. We want to know what Redwood has for evidence and how keys are managed.
00:00:58 Ethan: Great. We have SOC2 Type II, and we can provide the report under an NDA. We'll send a summary and the attestation link after this call. For keys, we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS in hosted and dedicated — or HSM-backed keys for Private.
00:01:12 Zoe: When you say customer-managed keys in hosted, is that envelope encryption where Redwood never sees the plaintext key? Or do you hold a copy?
00:01:20 Priya: Good question. In our hosted flow you can bring your own KMS key (BYOK) — Redwood holds only ciphertext; we use envelope encryption and ephemeral data keys. Priya: There is a key rotation process and audit trail. For Private, you manage the entire HSM.
00:01:36 Noah: What about key rotation frequency and rotation impact on cached KV entries? We can't afford large cache invalidations.
00:01:44 Priya: For KV cache we separate token encryption from model KV cache integrity. Rotation is done via re-wrapping rather than decrypt-reencrypt for cached state, usually zero-downtime if configured with dual-wraps. Might be a bit, uh, technical, happy to walk offline and show sequence diagram.
00:02:02 Liam: Okay that's promising. Next — SSO and SAML. We use Okta and SCIM to provision service accounts with fine-grained roles.
00:02:12 Ethan: Redwood supports SSO via SAML and OIDC and automated SCIM provisioning for user/role sync. On top of that we have RBAC that maps SCIM groups to platform roles; you can define custom roles for token level scoping.
00:02:25 Priya: Example: you can have a role that allows inference-only read tokens, another for model deploy and a third for admin. We also support short-lived API tokens tied to the identity provider session.
00:02:37 Priyanka: Do you support service accounts for nonhuman workloads that can be rotated via SCIM?
00:02:43 Priya: Yup — service accounts are supported, and SCIM handles lifecycle. Rotation can be automated with our recommended script.
00:02:50 Ava: Audit logs — we need to ingest into Splunk and retain logs for 2 years. What does Redwood surface and how do we get them?
00:02:59 Ethan: We emit structured audit logs for auth events, API calls, model changes, and billing events. Logs can stream to your SIEM via Kinesis/CloudWatch or delivered as S3 objects. Retention is configurable — for hosted we offer export pipelines; for Dedicated/Private you can control retention locally.
00:03:18 Zoe: Are full request/response payloads logged? We have PII concerns.
00:03:24 Priya: By default we log metadata and headers, not full prompt/response payloads. If you need full payload logging for debugging, that's an opt-in and we recommend scrubbing or tokenization. We also have field-level masking rules and a redaction API.
00:03:40 Liam: Good. Data residency: some assets must remain in EU. Do you have region pinning for models and logs?
00:03:47 Ethan: Yes, region pinning is supported. Hosted supports regional model hosting. Dedicated gives predictable capacity in chosen region. Private — fully customer-controlled network and region.
00:03:56 Noah: On networking, can Redwood do VPC peering or private link to our VPC? We want no public egress for inference calls.
00:04:05 Priya: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link options. Hosted has private endpoint support and VPC peering for enterprise tiers. Private is customer-hosted inside your VPC with no public egress. We'll share a sample VPC peering diagram.
00:04:18 Ava: That helps. Another angle — compliance frameworks beyond SOC2. We're exploring ISO 27001 and FedRAMP later. Any foothold?
00:04:26 Ethan: We have mapped controls to ISO 27001 and can share the gap map. FedRAMP is more involved — for now most customers choose Dedicated in a FedRAMP partner region or Private deployment.
00:04:36 Priyanka: On RBAC, how granular is RBAC for model-level access and token scoping? We need to separate teams so only certain groups can deploy or edit prompts.
00:04:45 Priya: Role model allows resource-level policies: project, model, route. You can bind roles to groups via SCIM. Also token-level scoping restricts routes and max tokens, and you can attach allowed models to tokens.
00:04:58 Liam: Is there auditability around token creation and token usage? We need per-token usage logs for billing and security auditing.
00:05:05 Ethan: Yes — token creation events are logged, as are usage metrics per token. We also support per-token cost/latency breakdown in the Console and can stream usage events to your billing system.
00:05:16 Zoe: Encryption at rest — we want AES-256, plus support for customer-managed KMS. Any customer key possible?
00:05:23 Priya: We use AES-GCM 256 for data at rest. For customer-managed keys we integrate with major KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). For HSM-backed keys on Private we support industry-standard PKCS11 HSMs.
00:05:36 Noah: Backups — are backups encrypted with same keys and what's retention?
00:05:41 Ethan: Backups are encrypted with the same KMS policy; retention is configurable and we can support purge windows. We'll include backup retention and restore SLAs in the security package.
00:05:52 Priyanka: There's also a subtle behavior with model rollback — model artifacts are immutable and signed; rollbacks don't expose previous plaintext. We can discuss artifact signing and verifiable provenance in the pilot.
00:06:05 Ava: Timeline and blockers — realistically what do you need from us to start a pilot?
00:06:11 Ethan: Minimums: SOC2 NDA review, sample traffic profile, network admin contact for VPC peering, and confirmation of key management preference (BYOK via your cloud KMS or Private HSM). After that we can stand up a Dedicated pilot in ~2-3 weeks.
00:06:25 Priya: We'll also want a brief performance benchmark — small script you run or we can run together — to validate latency targets with your sequence lengths.
00:06:34 Priyanka: For procurement: will there be a PO, or do we need a legal review first?
00:06:40 Zoe: Legal will want to see SOC2 and encryption details; procurement prefers a PO but we can start with a pilot under an MSA.
00:06:47 Carlos: Noted — we'll share our standard MSA template and the SOC2 package.
00:06:52 Liam: One more question: automated key revocation on employee offboarding — can you tie that to SCIM deprovisioning?
00:07:00 Priya: Yes, deprovisioning via SCIM triggers role removal and can trigger token revocation workflows. We also support automatic key rotation policies and programmatic key revocation hooks.
00:07:12 Ava: Okay that covers most of our high level. Appreciate the clarity.
00:07:16 Ethan: Recap / next steps: we'll send SOC2 Type II and ISO mapping, Priya will drop a VPC peering sketch and recommended RBAC mapping, and we need your sample traffic profile. We'll aim to get pilot kickoff scheduled the week of Feb 22.
00:07:30 Priyanka: I'll also put together a short runbook for key management options and a note about audit log delivery methods.
00:07:38 Noah: I'll share retention requirements and the list of log sinks we use.
00:07:44 Ethan: Great. Any other blockers?
00:07:47 Ava: Not on our side. Thank you.
00:07:49 Ethan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
